identification: John Campbell Pottery, Launceston. Shield-shaped wall pocket, catalogue height 18 cm (other examples measured 18 to 18.5 x 14.5 x 5.5 cm). Front: mottled emerald to aqua green glaze; relief koala in treacle brown clinging to a gum branch, two brown gumnuts above, leaves picked out in ochre yellow. Back: flat, olive yellow-green glaze with darker green runs at the edges, three stilt marks. No shape number, no date. The koala, nuts, branch and leaves are identical on the ten other examples I compared (Leski 2024 and 2026, Mossgreen 2009 x2 and 2016, Shapiro 2007 and 2015, Gowans 2011, eBay 2025 and 2026, Albion 2026), so the decoration is moulded, not hand-modelled; only the glaze colours change. Made after John Campbell's death in 1929, when his son Colin ran the pottery: about 1930s to 1950s. No dated example found. Condition from photos: pale angular marks on the front near the top rim, left of the gumnuts (possible glaze flake or chip, could be reflections); a dark brown spot on the side edge (right side from the front, left from the back): chip, kiln mark or glaze burn. No crack visible. Current bid $200 on 28 Nov 2026.

viewing_check: Top rim and the area left of the gumnuts: chip, glaze flake or hairline? Use a torch and a fingernail.
The brown spot on the side edge: a chip through the glaze, or a kiln mark?
Read the gold oval label on the front (pottery or retailer?) and confirm the incised initials read K.B.L.
